items.title: Australian couple trapped in Argentina with no legal rights to biological child
items.description: Jonathan and Amy had a child via surrogacy in Argentina. They have been stuck there for 12 months, unable to bring their daughter home.

items.title: Ukraine reclaims more than 200km of territory in five days
items.description: Ukraine has made its largest battlefield gains in more than two and a half years, retaking more than 200 square kilometres of its territory from Russia in just five days, according to a new analysis.

items.title: As solar booms, an Australian technology is rolled out around the world
items.description: At the interface of AI, big data, the energy transition and mind-bogglingly complex weather systems, the ongoing supply of electricity relies on answering a deceptively simple question: Will it be sunny?

items.title: As Sisonke held what police say was an IED, she waited for them to act
items.description: When Sisonke picked up a device that looked like a glass jar in Perth on Australia Day, she had a sense of foreboding so she took it to police. She says they took some time to act.

items.title: Live: Burke confirms Australians in Syria linked with ISIS have passports
items.description: Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has confirmed the Australians in Syria linked with ISIS fighters have been issued passports. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Terrifying crash in slopestyle final leaves Aussie teenager nursing bruised sternum
items.description: Ally Hickman's slopestyle final is halted by a frightening crash that leaves her motionless on the course as Danielle Scott delivers Australia its sixth medal of the Winter Olympics. Follow live.

items.title: Dani Scott's tears of joy a welcome balm after years of pain
items.description: As anxiety builds in this most tension-filled Winter Olympic sport, it's no wonder tears are a by product of both success and failure. Thankfully for Dani Scott, this time she was crying tears of pure joy.

items.title: Australia set for highest government debt levels since World War II
items.description: Australia will cease to be a low-debt country and be more vulnerable in a future crisis without a combination of spending restraint and tax reform, a new report has warned.

items.title: Climate disinformation, the Atlas Network and Dr Karl
items.description: The scourge of AI-slopaganda, viral disinformation campaigns, and online attacks against individuals and institutions is going to get far worse before it gets better, if the latest public hearings on the topic are any indication.

items.title: 'Blatant' fake discounting by retailers in ACCC's sights
items.description: ACCC chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb outlines the consumer watchdog's priorities for 2026, including targeting "blatant" fake discounting.

items.title: Victoria loses MotoGP after almost 30 years at Phillip Island
items.description: Victoria loses the rights to host the Australian Motorcycle Grand Prix, ending a three-decade association with the event.

items.title: Documents reveal messages between Chinese official and accused spy trio
items.description: The police case relies on WeChat communication allegedly between the trio in Australia and a person at China's Public Security Bureau.

items.title: Eight back-country skiers found dead, one missing after avalanche in California
items.description: Eight skiers have been found dead and one is missing after an avalanche in California, making it the deadliest avalanche in the US in forty years.

items.title: Trump official says US did not censor Colbert interview but is probing The View
items.description: The confirmation of a probe into the daytime talk show came after it interviewed the same Democratic candidate whose interview with Stephen Colbert was allegedly barred from airing.

items.title: He helped discover Antarctica but lies in an unmarked grave — until today
items.description: Captain John King Davis was one of Australia's greatest Antarctic explorers, but for decades, his final resting place was an unmarked grave in Melbourne. Today, that will change.

items.title: Trainspotting: How Britpop and beats shaped an era-defining soundtrack
items.description: Most films are lucky to get just one needle-drop moment embedded in the Zeitgeist. Trainspotting boasted several.

items.title: Why a country council paid $3.4m for a pool it didn't want
items.description: A Victorian community group promised its local shire a new pool would not cost it money once it was built. In less than three months, the promise was broken.

items.title: Former Fiji PM and police chief charged with inciting mutiny
items.description: Long-serving Fiji prime minister Frank Bainimarama and a former police commissioner will face court on Tuesday on charges of mutiny.

items.title: Residents creating water out of thin air as they wait for 'basic right'
items.description: Just three hours from Brisbane, the residents of Cherbourg need to boil the town water to make it safe to drink. Delays to a new water treatment plant have driven them to use emerging technology that creates clean water from thin air.

items.title: Car suspected of chasing truck on wrong side of Bruce Highway before fatal crash found
items.description: A Narangba man is now assisting police with their investigation into Tuesday's fatal crash.

items.title: Live: ASX set to follow Wall Street higher ahead of busy results day, oil surges
items.description: Wall Street's rise is expected to flow through to ASX as heavyweights Telstra, Wesfarmers and Goodman report this morning. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: This town lost its aged care home. Now locals have taken back the keys
items.description: Residents of a Victorian country town have taken over their aged care home, but now have to work out how to run it.

items.title: Religious and union groups worry about proposed ban on certain phrases
items.description: Religious groups and unions have expressed their concern about a Queensland government move to ban the use of certain phrases as part of an antisemitism crackdown.

items.title: Sydney mental health patients who fled care accused of killing three people
items.description: A driver charged over a double-fatal crash used a staff pass to escape hospital the day before an alleged Sydney stabber fled the same mental health facility.

items.title: Push for greater action on CFMEU scandal from within premier's own team
items.description: Pressure on Jacinta Allan intensifies, with several of the premier's own MPs saying they want to see a royal commission into alleged criminality and corruption within the Construction, Forestry and Maritime Employees Union.
